dedupe_keys.name: nlr evi pro electric vehicle infrastructure projection tool charging port needs and grid load from light duty travel patterns

description: EVI-Pro is the National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL) tool that estimates how much electric vehicle charging infrastructure an area needs to meet a given demand. Contents: developed with the California Energy Commission, it uses detailed data on personal vehicle travel patterns, EV attributes and charging station characteristics to analyse typical daily light-duty travel, estimate charging demand and design infrastructure to meet it, accounting for vehicle and charger technologies, demographics, market adoption, shared use of chargers and charging preferences. A simplified web version, EVI-Pro Lite, lets US cities and states estimate charging needs and the associated power demand on the grid. Producer: NLR Transportation and Mobility Research, part of the EVI-X suite. Coverage: United States; published applications include the 2030 national charging network study (2023), California (2021), Maryland (2019), Columbus, Ohio (2018) and Massachusetts (2017). Format and access: EVI-Pro Lite is a free web tool; the full model is used in NLR analyses and partnerships (contact evi-x@nlr.gov). Licence: not stated on the NLR page. Caveats: results depend on assumed adoption and travel behaviour; the full tool is not a public download. Simulation uses: sizing public and home charging networks and estimating charging load profiles for distribution and bulk grid planning. Related records: platform-nlr-evi-x-ev-charging-infrastructure-modelling-suite and data-doe-ev-data-collection-charging.
